taxonomy.subtopic: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling and antiangiogenic endothelial injury

questions.stem_html:
A previously normotensive 29-year-old primigravida at 31 weeks has blood pressure readings of 166/104 and 162/102 mm Hg, new proteinuria, headache, and elevated liver transaminases. Doppler assessment earlier in pregnancy showed high-resistance uterine arterial flow. Laboratory testing demonstrates increased soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1.

Which placental abnormality initiated the maternal syndrome?

options.text_html: Incomplete trophoblastic remodeling of spiral arteries, causing placental hypoperfusion and release of antiangiogenic factors
Excessive invasion of trophoblasts through the myometrium and serosa
Failure of the neural tube to close during embryogenesis
Maternal production of antibodies against fetal red-cell antigens
Premature senescence of the corpus luteum with progesterone withdrawal

questions.explanation_html: Shallow trophoblast invasion leaves spiral arteries narrow and high resistance. Placental ischemia promotes release of sFlt-1 and other factors that antagonize VEGF/PlGF, causing widespread maternal endothelial dysfunction. Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling is the initiating placental lesion that links high-resistance flow to antiangiogenic factor release and maternal disease.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Excessive trophoblastic invasion is associated with placenta accreta spectrum, not preeclampsia.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Neural-tube defects do not cause the maternal endothelial syndrome of preeclampsia.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Red-cell alloimmunization causes fetal hemolysis rather than maternal hypertension and proteinuria.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Placental hormone production maintains pregnancy after the first trimester; corpus-luteum failure is not the mechanism of late preeclampsia.

questions.educational_objective: Trace preeclampsia from defective spiral-artery remodeling to placental ischemia, sFlt-1 excess, systemic endothelial dysfunction, hypertension, and proteinuria.
